title: Signal QuickLog: annotated anchors & minimal fixes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This quicklog is a compact, annotated roll-up of recent direct-customer threads (support, AM calls, and field notes) where customers surfaced small but high-confidence asks. The goal: produce 6–10 minimal-scope probes (<=2w eng + 1 CS validation) that reduce friction or unblock purchases for mid-market and enterprise buyers.

How to read this doc:
- Each entry = customer vignette + signal -> root-cause hypothesis -> one-line minimal fix -> effort/impact T-shirt -> suggested owner / follow-up ticket.
- Annotations in [brackets] are CS/SE color commentary (quick).
- Prioritization is pragmatic: high-impact means visible business blocker or purchase gating.

Entries (chronological):

2026-03-02 | "Nimbus Health" (enterprise, Private pilot)
Quote: "We saw response spikes when the worker node rotated—cache resets and tokens blow our cost estimates."
Signal: Observed latency/cost spikes tied to model warm-starts and KV cache invalidation after pod restarts.
Hypothesis: Customer is sensitive to transient token regen and KV cache cold-starts; their workload uses long-running chat sessions pinned to user IDs causing frequent cache churn when infrastructure scales.
Minimal fix: Add a 1) lightweight per-tenant KV snapshot/export on controlled drain so serving can pre-warm on the target host; 2) UI toggle in Console (Pilot-only) to enable "preserve-KV-on-drain".
Effort/Impact: M (2w eng + Console flag); Impact = H (reduces cost/cliff for private pilots; increases chance to convert to Dedicated).
Suggested owner / ticket: eng-serving-runtime -> JIRA-CS-889 follow-up.
Notes: [Dev note: prototype uses existing KV checkpoint hooks; check SRE runbook for drains. CS to ask customer for exact restart cadence and session-stickiness patterns.]

2026-03-05 | "WriteFlow" (PLG startup using Hosted API)
Quote: "We get hallucinated navigation suggestions when using model-variants with quantized kernels."
Signal: Quality regression after model-variant fallback to 4-bit quantized edition under autoscaling pressure.
Hypothesis: Quantized model variant not covered by prompt-safety tests and has slightly different tokenization edge cases -> output drift for system prompts with tight constraints.
Minimal fix: Add a quick quality-guard that compares top-k logits for critical prompt set (n=20 short prompts) before serving fallback variant; if divergence > threshold, route to warm-hosted baseline model (slower but better).
Effort/Impact: S (1w runtime + test harness); Impact = M (reduces customer-visible hallucinations, small latency cost in fallback).
Suggested owner / ticket: product-hosted-api prototype GH-PR-5126.
Notes: [We already have eval infra in Optimize team; ask for shared small prompt-set from customer.]

2026-03-09 | "ScribeOps" (platform team, Dedicated customer)
Quote: "Rollouts are unclear — who gets the new tokenizer? Why did devs see different generation behavior?"
Signal: Confusion around rollout semantics for tokenizer/compilation changes across variants. Customers treat tokenization changes as model-breaking.
Hypothesis: Rollout UI and rollout notes don't clearly surface non-backwards-compatible compiler/kernel changes; rollout docs assume same tokenization across model versions.
Minimal fix: Add a short, auto-generated "compatibility summary" banner on rollout pages showing: tokenization change (Y/N), kv-cache compatibility (Y/N), recommended canary % if tokenization changed.
Effort/Impact: S (UI + small backend metadata flagging); Impact = H (reduces support overhead, speeds canary signoff).
Suggested owner / ticket: product/console-and-rollouts -> create ticket.

2026-03-11 | "LegalCloud" (regulated financial services, Private eval)
Quote: "We need guaranteed audit trail for inference requests tied to CMK usage — our compliance team needs >90d immutable logs."
Signal: Compliance ask for longer-term immutable audit retention tied to KMS events when Private deployed.
Hypothesis: Private-deploy default log retention is shorter and lacks the KMS-tied immutable flag the customer expects.
Minimal fix: Build a documentation + configuration recipe for Private that wires Redwood logging to customer S3/GCS with object immutability turned on, and add an opt-in setting in Private install manifest to mark logs immutable.
Effort/Impact: S (docs + helm value + 1 engineer consult); Impact = H (unblocks purchase for regulated customers).
Suggested owner / ticket: private-deployments + security-and-compliance.
Notes: [This is mostly packaging + docs; ask Solutions Eng for a prebuilt manifest].

2026-03-12 | "SynthRetail" (customer success trial)
Quote: "Batching kills our tail-latency for small interactive flows — users hit a timeout on 2s SLA."
Signal: Autoscaling batching/enqueue policy causing requests to wait for batch formation even for low qps tasks.
Hypothesis: Default batch latency targets favor throughput; interactive flows would prefer single-request fast-path.
Minimal fix: Add a per-route toggle (Console + API) "prefer-latency-over-throughput" that sets a smaller batch window and a hard single-request fallback after X ms.
Effort/Impact: M (1.5w runtime + console toggle); Impact = H for PLG interactive features.
Suggested owner / ticket: serving-runtime feature request.

2026-03-13 | "EduPrompt" (developer sandbox)
Quote: "Embedding drift is causing search mismatch after model refresh — we lost several results."
Signal: Embedding model upgrades not accompanied by an automatic reindex or clear migration path.
Hypothesis: Customers expect a migration recipe (recompute embeddings incrementally) and a simple way to tag old embeddings as compatible.
Minimal fix: Ship a "reindex advisor" script in SDK: scans dataset, surfaces estimated cost/time, and generates an incremental recompute plan (batch size, checkpoint) with a one-command runner.
Effort/Impact: S (1w SDK + docs); Impact = M (reduces obstacles for small companies to adopt newer embedding models).
Suggested owner / ticket: developer-experience + product-optimize.

Cross-cutting observations (short):
- Many asks are smallish UX/operational knobs rather than deep runtime rework. Quick wins usually live in Console toggles + small runtime flags.
- Customers repeatedly ask for clearer compatibility metadata when models/compilation change. This is low-hanging and high-value.
- Private deployments surface ops/packaging asks (log immutability, KMS binding) that can be productized as install-time recipe templates.

Unresolved questions and research probes:
- How many Private customers would enable persisted KV-on-drain by default? (ask AMs: Diego + Priya)
- What's the realistic SLA tradeoff customers accept when we fallback from quantized variant to baseline? Need telemetry sample from hosting infra.
- Can rollout pages reliably read compile-time metadata (tokenizer, kernel flags) from the model catalog? Quick spike with Model Onboarding team.

Proposed immediate next steps (0–7 days):
1) CS to validate priority: share this quicklog with top-6 pilots and ask for impact thumbs-up (Aisha).
2) Engineering quick spikes: one eng each for KV-on-drain, per-route latency toggle, and rollout-compat banner (owners volunteer in weekly sync).
3) Solutions Eng to produce a Private immutable-log manifest draft and attach to ticket.
4) DevEx to sketch the reindex-advisor CLI and attach sample PR with API surface.

Appendix: raw snippets from threads (redacted)
- "When a node drains, our TCO for the month jumped 20% — we traced it to repeated context re-sends." — Nimbus health engineer
- "After a quiet night the embed search started returning older results — we later learned the model variant was replaced in the catalog." — EduPrompt PM

Notes to self:
- Keep these entries dense. Avoid re-running full VOC clustering for microfixes; instead aim for validated microproposals.
- Flag anything needing >3w as "program-level" and push to product roadmap sync.

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.ai) — ping in #cs-field-signals for follow-up.

Document history: created 2026-03-14; synthesized from CS tickets and AM call notes (Mar 2–13).
